source.title: Memorisation, convergence and generalisation in generative models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures memorization and generalization in generative models, not the supervised natural-label train/test behavior or any specific version in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper's generative-model findings concern different measures and settings from the claim versions; none of the versions is tested.
record.test_reason: The study measures generated-sample memorization, agreement between independently fitted generative models, and latent-subspace recovery. These results do not test any of V1–V8. The introduction cites supervised generalization findings as background; its generative-model arguments do not challenge those specific claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors distinguish bulk-distribution agreement from consistent recovery of principal latent factors, connect them to different statistical distances in their Gaussian setting, and report related distinctions on real images and diffusion samples. They leave extensions beyond Gaussian models and static estimators open.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes generative-model memorization, output convergence, and latent recovery rather than supervised classification train/test error on natural and random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: In the real-image diffusion comparison, the rotated overlap Q⋆ depends on the chosen basis; the paper contrasts a vanilla U-Net and standard sampling with Kadkhodaie et al.'s blind denoiser and sampling algorithm.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear Gaussian generative models show decreasing generated-sample memorization, continuous output convergence, and a separate threshold for principal-subspace recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generated-sample memorization, output convergence, and latent recovery are distinct properties with different sample-complexity behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Output convergence bounds rescaled excess KL divergence, while principal-subspace recovery governs asymptotic excess maximum-sliced distance in the specified spiked Gaussian regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different distributional distances track different aspects of generative-model learning.

fits_no_version.finding: On real images, Fourier correlation-subspace overlap shows a sharp transition and is suppressed by phase randomization; related transitions appear in diffusion-generated images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A basis-dependent correlation-subspace measure can distinguish latent recovery from agreement driven by the spectral envelope.

record.problems: Several image and diffusion findings are reported in figures without exact numerical values in the text. The authors identify limits including Gaussian assumptions, static estimators, and the need to extend the analysis beyond the studied setting.

untested.parts: Random-label training fit, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels under matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifier test error and the contribution of learned or imposed local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address different constructs; this does not negate the reported generative-model findings. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fitting random labels and generalizing on natural labels in supervised classifiers.
The paper does not sweep network width past the interpolation threshold in supervised learning.
The paper does not compare convolutional and fully connected classifiers.
The paper does not compare adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers on supervised benchmarks.
The paper does not compare batch sizes or train/test gaps under fixed epoch budgets.
The paper does not test dropout effects on supervised classification error.
The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps in supervised networks.
The paper does not remove influential memorized training examples and measure the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: Linear generative model
rows.size_stated: input dimension d; sample size n
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximal normalized overlap between generated samples and training examples as sample size increases.

conditions.value: n = Θ(1), then n ≫ 1 after d → ∞

rows.value: For n = 1, m = 1; for n ≫ 1 after d → ∞, m ≃ √(2 log n / [n(1 + σ²)]).
rows.note: The paper describes memorization of training examples by a generative model; this is not supervised random-label fitting.
rows.check: Generated-sample overlap does not measure V1's random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy. Also, the main text's unconditional n=1, m=1 statement conflicts with equation A.9: for positive regularization, that equation gives E[|Z|/sqrt(Z²+σ²)]<1. Qualify perfect memorization to σ=0.

rows.subject: Linear generative models trained on independent datasets
rows.size_stated: input dimension d; sample size n
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap of outputs from independently estimated generative models given the same latent.
rows.value: q = [Eγ√(λ + σ²)]² / (1 + σ²) + o(1); q rises continuously from zero to one as n/d increases.
rows.note: The result concerns agreement between generated outputs, not classification test error.
rows.check: Output agreement does not measure any claim version. The zero-to-one description requires σ=0: equation A.18 gives q→σ²/(1+σ²) as γ→0 for fixed positive σ.

rows.subject: Linear generative models trained on independent datasets
rows.size_stated: input dimension d; sample size n
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap between top empirical covariance eigenvectors from independent datasets.

conditions.value: Gaussian inputs with rank-one spiked covariance

rows.value: Q = δ(γ)² + o(1) when γ ≥ β⁻²; Q → 1 as γ → ∞.
rows.note: The paper finds a threshold for latent recovery distinct from the continuous rise of q.
rows.check: Principal-subspace recovery is outside V1–V8. The threshold formula is correctly recorded; Q→1 requires β>0.

rows.subject: Linear generative model
rows.size_stated: input dimension d; sample size n
rows.operation_detail: Compared convergence overlap with rescaled excess KL divergence between true and estimated distributions.

conditions.value: Gaussian distribution; leading-order analysis sets β = 0
Two σ values, not stated in text

rows.value: −½ log q ≤ D ≤ 2[1 + log(1 + σ⁻²)](1 − q). For n < d, D is almost stationary; for n > d, it decays with sample complexity as a power law.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative regimes and bounds; plotted parameter values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: Distributional KL divergence does not measure any claim version. Specify that D compares the fitted distribution with the regularized true distribution, rather than the unregularized truth.

rows.subject: Linear generative model
rows.size_stated: input dimension d; sample size n
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum-sliced distance and related its decay to principal-subspace overlap.
rows.note: This is a distributional distance in a generative-model setting.
rows.check: Maximum-sliced distance is outside V1–V8. The derivation in section B.3 concerns excess distance with matching regularization on the true and estimated covariances; that qualification should accompany the formula.

rows.subject: Linear generative model fitted to CelebA images
rows.operation_detail: Measured convergence and top-eigenvector overlap across independently sampled disjoint subsets.
rows.measure: Convergence overlap q and subspace overlap Q
rows.value: Q attains large values for a small number of samples and continues to increase continuously; q and Q are plotted in Figure 3(b).
rows.note: The description gives the qualitative result; exact plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: Covariance-based output and eigenvector overlaps do not test classifier generalization. Split q and Q into separate measure rows. Figure 3 specifies widths {16,32,64}, whereas section C.1 specifies {32,48,64}; the source is internally inconsistent.

rows.subject: Linear generative model fitted to CelebA images
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap between leading eigenvectors of Fourier-space correlation matrices across disjoint datasets.
rows.value: Q⋆ undergoes a sharp transition as sample complexity increases.
rows.note: The authors state that Q⋆ depends on the choice of rotation basis.
rows.check: Fourier correlation-subspace recovery is outside V1–V8. The reported transition is supported, but image widths differ between Figure 3 and section C.1.

rows.subject: Linear generative model fitted to CelebA images with randomized Fourier phases
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlaps after randomizing each image's Fourier-coefficient phases.

conditions.value: Randomized phases preserve the power-law spectrum while destroying Fourier-space correlations

rows.baseline: Original CelebA images; exact values not stated
rows.value: Q⋆ remains close to zero, while q and Q remain unaffected.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a control for latent correlation structure.
rows.check: The phase-randomization control tests a generative-model metric, not a claim version. Split the three measures: Q⋆ stays near zero, while q and Q are described as unaffected.

rows.subject: Diffusion models trained independently on disjoint CelebA subsets
rows.size_stated: U-Net; batch size 512; about 200k training steps
rows.operation_detail: Measured memorization and convergence overlaps on generated images as training-subset size increased.
rows.measure: Memorization overlap m and convergence overlap q
rows.value: The paper reports a transition from memorization to convergence as n increases; plotted histograms are in Figure D.1.
rows.note: Figure D.1 shows four repetitions per sample complexity; exact overlap values are not stated.
rows.check: Generated-image memorization and convergence are distinct from V1's supervised-label experiment. Split m and q into separate rows. Figure D.1 specifies subset sizes n={10,100,1000,10000,100000} and four repetitions.

rows.subject: Diffusion models trained independently on disjoint CelebA subsets
rows.size_stated: U-Net; batch size 512; about 200k training steps
rows.operation_detail: Measured convergence, naïve subspace, and rotated subspace overlaps on generated images.

conditions.value: Vanilla U-Net denoiser and standard DDPM sampling
Images generated by the authors' models and images from Kadkhodaie et al.

rows.value: Q is uninformative on generated samples; Q⋆ exhibits a sharp transition for both the authors' models and the images from Kadkhodaie et al.
rows.uncertainty: Average and error in the mean over four runs per sample complexity for the authors' models
rows.note: The authors used a standard U-Net and sampling procedure; Kadkhodaie et al. used a blind denoiser and a different sampling algorithm.
rows.check: These overlaps do not test V1–V8. Split the measures and the two model sources: Figure 4(a) uses the authors' U-Net/DDPM models; Figure 4(b) reanalyzes images supplied by Kadkhodaie et al. The authors' batch size, training steps, and four-run uncertainty do not describe the latter models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
